newsitem.title: USA: Ethics panel sets Gingrich sanctions sessions.
newsitem.headline: Ethics panel sets Gingrich sanctions sessions.

text.p: The House ethics committee announced early on Thursday a week-long schedule of hearings leading up to a decision on the punishment to be meted out to Speaker Newt Gingrich for violating House rules.

After day-long negotiations behind closed doors, the committee said that lawyers for the committee and Gingrich would address a hearing set to take place from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Monday. Subsequent hearings will be held through the week, ending on Friday. The committee is to report to the full House no later than Sunday, Jan. 19.
Speculation is that the committee will recommend that the full House reprimand Gingrich -- a punishment below the level of expulsion and censure.

Following the two counsels' presentations on Monday, further hearings will be used to enable members to supplement the record and question the lawyers. After that, each counsel will make recommendations on what sanctions should be imposed.

"The committee anticipates completing its deliberations by January 17, 1997," a committee statement said. "In any event, the committee shall report to the House the information brought out during the sanction hearing, the committee's recommended sanction and the reasons therefore not later than January 19, 1997," the statement said.

Gingrich admitted he failed to get legal advice to ensure compliance with a ban on using tax-exempt funds for partisan political activity and had given false information to investigators, which he said was unintentional.
